title: MEXC Releases September–October Security Report: Guardian Fund Adds 1,000 BTC, Reserve Ratios Exceed 100%
summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 24, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released its September–October 2026 security report. The report shows that the MEXC Guardian Fund increased its BTC holdings to 2,000 BTC, while reserve ratios for four major assets—BTC, ETH, USDT, and USDC—remained above 100%. The crypto industry faces security challenges across multiple points of exposure. The report recorded 196 security incidents in September–October, with total asset losses exceeding $7.3 billion. Several large-scale incidents involved breaches of exchange wallets and transaction signing systems that enabled unauthorized asset transfers. Attackers used fake recruitment campaigns to persuade employees to download malware, exploited vulnerabilities in third-party tools to steal internal credentials, and distributed phishing links through compromised official accounts. These incidents have drawn greater attention to platforms’ access controls and reserve transparency. Guardian Fund Adds 1,000 BTC In September 2026, MEXC allocated an additional 1,000 BTC to the Guardian Fund, marking its second addition of the year. By the end of September, the fund held 2,000 BTC and more than 100 million USDT, maintaining reserves in both BTC and USDT. The Guardian Fund is designed to support user protection in serious security incidents, including major exploits, targeted attacks, and unforeseen system vulnerabilities. The latest addition follows MEXC’s plan, announced in May 2026, to expand the fund to $500 million within two years. MEXC has published the fund’s holding addresses so users can review on-chain balances and transaction records: USDT Reserve Address (Ethereum): 0x469AfE803C54A36674C55231489Cf4b61da8c1bC First BTC Reserve Address: 1MDVjZdX8QD212pT8Z8EMP7DuFQHKqN3mx Second BTC Reserve Address: 19KYQDpyssRUtpfa4pfAWiNQLeysThd1us Reserve Ratios Exceed 100% for All Four Assets MEXC’s October 9, 2026 reserve snapshot showed reserve ratios above 100% for all four major assets disclosed. The BTC reserve ratio stood at 293.86%, with wallet assets of 12,402.93 BTC against user assets of 4,220.56 BTC. The ETH reserve ratio was 110.90%, with wallet assets of 59,691.16 ETH against user assets of 53,820.65 ETH. USDT and USDC reserve ratios were 122.38% and 115.42%, respectively. Users can review platform wallet and user asset data on the MEXC Proof of Reserves and Asset Protection page and use Merkle tree verification to check whether their account balances are included in that reserve snapshot. Futures Insurance Fund Reaches 830 Million USDT to Help Cover Liquidation Deficits As of November 5, 2026, the MEXC Futures Insurance Fund held 830,411,315 USDT. This was an increase of 38,714,893 USDT, or 4.89%, from the September 1 balance disclosed in the previous report. The Futures Insurance Fund covers deficits caused by insufficient margin during forced liquidation. It provides a financial buffer during sharp market swings and helps reduce the risk of triggering auto-deleveraging (ADL). Users can view the fund balance and historical changes on the MEXC Trust page. MEXC Returns More Than 1 Million USDT in Erroneous Deposits MEXC helps users recover assets deposited in error. In September–October, its customer service team manually completed 1,354 returns of erroneous deposits, returning assets worth 1,002,660 USDT. Compared with July–August, the number of completed returns increased 65.5%, while the value of assets returned rose 66.5%. MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said, “In the AI era, attackers can find vulnerabilities and develop attacks faster. Exchanges must also upgrade their technical defenses, strengthen internal controls, and improve their incident response capabilities. MEXC will continue to invest in security, build up its protection reserves, and regularly report on progress in user protection. Through sustained security investment and transparent disclosure, we aim to build lasting trust with our users.” About MEXC Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway. With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity. title: Binance Hack: US Moves to Recover $1.1 Billion, but Who Gets the Money?
summary: Key takeaways US authorities filed a civil forfeiture complaint on November 23 seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October 29 Binance hack, across 36 addresses on 18 blockchains. Circle froze the funds but says it cannot technically move them, so it proposes issuing replacement USDC to the US after a forfeiture order. Frozen is not recovered: the filings advance the legal-control stage, while final distribution and ownership remain undecided. A separate Abu Dhabi court order adds a second jurisdiction, and Circle’s reserve and supply reporting for the replacement tokens will deserve scrutiny. Nearly four weeks after the Binance hack, US authorities have filed a civil forfeiture complaint seeking more than $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the October theft. The money is already subject to restrictions, but the latest court filings reveal a complication: freezing stolen cryptocurrency is considerably easier than returning it. The complaint, filed on November 23, in the US District Court for the District of Columbia, targets USDC associated with 36 cryptocurrency addresses across 18 blockchains. Federal investigators attribute the October 29 attack to North Korean hacking groups, including the Lazarus Group. The complaint puts the value of the original theft at approximately $6 billion. For Binance, the latest legal action represents another opportunity to recover a portion of its losses. For the wider cryptocurrency industry, however, the case raises questions about the authority stablecoin issuers exercise over digital assets and what happens when governments become involved. Binance Hack Recovery Enters a New Legal Phase The assets targeted by US authorities are not an entirely new discovery. Earlier this month, NewsBTC reported that Circle had frozen approximately $1.1 billion in USDC linked to the Binance hack, following cooperation with law enforcement. What has changed is the government’s attempt to establish a legal basis for taking possession of those assets. According to the court documents, US authorities obtained a temporary restraining order on November 12. Prosecutors subsequently requested that the restrictions remain in place throughout the civil forfeiture proceedings. Both Binance and Circle consented to the initial restraining order and the requested extension, according to the government’s November 23 application. The agreement between the companies and federal authorities reduces one immediate obstacle to preserving the funds. It does not, however, resolve the question of their ultimate ownership or distribution. Civil forfeiture proceedings are directed against property believed to be connected to criminal activity. Interested parties can assert legitimate claims to that property through the legal process. In this case, prosecutors are seeking forfeiture of the assets to the United States. That is not the same thing as a court ordering their immediate return to Binance. Circle Cannot Simply Send the Frozen USDC Back Perhaps the most interesting disclosure in the complaint concerns Circle itself. The stablecoin issuer can restrict transfers involving USDC held at particular blockchain addresses. However, that authority does not necessarily give Circle direct control over the wallets holding those tokens. The complaint states that Circle: “ does not have the technical ability to transfer the Defendant Property from the blocklisted Subject Addresses to the United States US forfeiture complaint · November 23 filing Instead, Circle has agreed to issue an equivalent amount of replacement USDC and transfer those tokens to US authorities upon receiving a forfeiture order from the court. The proposed arrangement exposes an unusual feature of centralized stablecoins. An issuer can prevent tokens from circulating without possessing the private keys needed to move them. It also raises an accounting question that deserves attention. If replacement tokens are issued, what ultimately happens to the original frozen USDC, and how will Circle ensure that the treatment of those balances is reflected accurately in its outstanding supply and reserve reporting? The issuance of replacement tokens would not, by itself, prove that USDC had become undercollateralized. Nevertheless, transparency around the implementation would be important for a stablecoin whose credibility depends on confidence in its backing. The immediate concern is not whether Circle can create new tokens. It is whether the entire recovery process can be independently accounted for. The $1.1 Billion Is Not Back With Binance Yet The temptation to describe the Justice Department’s announcement as a billion-dollar recovery is understandable. It is also premature. There are three separate stages involved: restricting access to the stolen assets, obtaining legal authority over them and determining how they will ultimately be distributed. The November 23 filings advance the second stage. They do not establish that the third has been completed. The $1.1 billion Binance recovery process. Source: US District Court for the District of Columbia filings, November 23, 2026. There is also a cross-border complication. On November 18, Reuters reported that an Abu Dhabi court had directed several cryptocurrency companies, including Circle, to preserve digital assets associated with the Binance theft. The involvement of authorities in both the United States and the United Arab Emirates illustrates how a single cryptocurrency theft can generate legal proceedings across multiple jurisdictions. Blockchain transactions may cross national borders without much difficulty. Establishing ownership rights over the assets involved is a considerably less straightforward exercise. That does not mean the US and UAE proceedings are necessarily in conflict. But the ultimate disposition of the funds will require more than an announcement from either government. For investors assessing Binance’s financial position, the distinction between frozen assets and recovered capital is particularly important. Restricted cryptocurrency should not automatically be treated as money already returned to the exchange. The Binance Hack Tests the Case for Centralized Stablecoins For years, the ability of stablecoin issuers to freeze tokens has been criticized by advocates of decentralized finance. The Binance case demonstrates the other side of that argument. Without Circle’s ability to restrict transactions, preserving such a large amount of cryptocurrency for potential recovery would have been more difficult. In this particular case, centralized control has provided a mechanism that may help prevent suspected criminals from benefiting from stolen assets. The uncomfortable question is whether the cryptocurrency industry can benefit from that authority while also demanding meaningful safeguards against its misuse. The answer depends partly on transparency. Token holders should be able to understand why assets were frozen, under what legal authority restrictions remain in place and how disputes over ownership are resolved. The same standard should apply to the exchange, the stablecoin issuer and the government. The next significant development in the Binance case will be the court’s treatment of the forfeiture claim and any competing claims to the assets. Circle’s proposed issuance of replacement USDC will also deserve scrutiny if it proceeds. Until then, the $1.1 billion should be understood as assets subject to an ongoing recovery effort, not a completed repayment. For a cryptocurrency industry that frequently celebrates the speed of moving money, the Binance hack is a reminder that getting it back can be an entirely different business.

title: Bitcoin Reserves Just Found a New Use on Wall Street, but There’s a Catch
summary: Key takeaways CFTC staff guidance issued on November 23 says swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and clearinghouses may count Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. The advisory references a minimum 20% haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, so a $10 million Bitcoin reserve would count as $8 million, and 2% for qualifying payment stablecoins. Crypto cannot be used to meet the separate cash and liquid-resources requirement, which covers three months for swap execution facilities and generally six months for the other two types of venue. It is a staff advisory, not a binding rule, and nothing in it requires institutions to buy Bitcoin. Bitcoin reserves have found another potential use within the US financial system. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has clarified that regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses can count Bitcoin, Ethereum and qualifying payment stablecoins toward certain financial resource requirements. However, the regulator is not prepared to treat those holdings like cash. The guidance, issued on November 23, could give regulated trading venues greater flexibility in managing their balance sheets. For Bitcoin investors, however, the more interesting question is whether that flexibility will translate into fresh institutional demand. The answer is not quite as straightforward as it might seem. CFTC Gives Bitcoin Reserves a New Role in Financial Markets The CFTC’s latest advisory addresses three types of regulated businesses: swap execution facilities, designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations. These institutions are required to maintain sufficient financial resources to cover at least one year of operating costs. Under the new staff guidance, Bitcoin, Ether and qualifying payment stablecoins may contribute toward those requirements, subject to appropriate valuation discounts. The announcement follows broader efforts to integrate digital assets into regulated financial infrastructure. NewsBTC previously reported on the CFTC’s guidance concerning tokenized collateral at clearinghouses, another area where traditional financial markets are gradually accommodating blockchain-based assets. This time, the discussion is not about what traders can post as collateral. It is about the assets that the institutions running those markets can rely on to keep their businesses operating. For a company that already holds Bitcoin, the clarification could make those holdings more useful from a regulatory standpoint. For businesses considering adding cryptocurrency to their balance sheets, it removes some uncertainty surrounding how those assets would be recognized. But that recognition comes at a discount! A $10 Million Bitcoin Reserve Is Worth $8 Million on Paper The CFTC advisory references a minimum 20% valuation haircut for Bitcoin and Ethereum, consistent with earlier staff treatment of proprietary cryptocurrency positions held by futures commission merchants. Qualifying payment stablecoins receive considerably more favorable treatment, with a referenced haircut of 2%. An exchange holding $10 million in Bitcoin, for example, would be able to count $8 million toward the relevant financial resource requirement if it applied a 20% haircut and no further deductions were necessary. The remaining $2 million is not a realized loss. It is a regulatory adjustment intended to account for the risk associated with holding a volatile asset. Crypto assets that are neither readily marketable nor qualifying payment stablecoins would generally face a 100% haircut, effectively excluding them from the calculation. Perhaps the most revealing part of the advisory is the regulator’s warning about what it calls wrong-way risk. The CFTC staff specifically states: “ A DCM should consider potential wrong-way risk CFTC staff · November 23 advisory For a cryptocurrency-focused exchange, that risk is particularly relevant. A prolonged Bitcoin sell-off could put pressure on trading revenues while simultaneously reducing the value of the assets the exchange relies on to support its operations. The problem is not simply that Bitcoin is volatile. It is that its value could deteriorate at precisely the moment a crypto business finds itself under financial pressure. A 20% valuation discount provides some protection against that scenario, but it is hardly a guarantee. The CFTC Is Still Drawing a Line Between Bitcoin and Cash Despite allowing digital assets to contribute toward broader operating resources, the CFTC has maintained a separate requirement for cash and highly liquid securities. Bitcoin, Ethereum and even qualifying payment stablecoins cannot be used to satisfy that particular obligation under the advisory. Swap execution facilities must maintain qualifying liquid resources sufficient to cover at least three months of projected operating expenses or the cost of winding down their operations, whichever is greater. For designated contract markets and derivatives clearing organizations, the operating-cost liquidity requirement generally covers at least six months. The distinction matters because an institution can have substantial assets on its balance sheet without necessarily having the cash available to meet immediate obligations. It is also worth noting that the guidance does not address whether cryptocurrencies can satisfy the separate financial resources that clearinghouses must maintain to cover clearing-member defaults. In effect, the CFTC is recognizing Bitcoin as an asset that can contribute to an institution’s financial strength without giving it the same regulatory standing as cash. That is a more cautious approach than some Bitcoin advocates might have hoped for, but arguably a more sustainable one for integrating cryptocurrency into financial infrastructure. Could the Decision Trigger More Institutional Bitcoin Buying? The bullish interpretation is relatively simple. If regulated financial institutions can derive greater utility from holding Bitcoin, more of them may eventually consider allocating capital to the cryptocurrency. There is some merit to that argument. The expansion of regulated crypto infrastructure has already brought digital assets closer to traditional financial markets. Earlier, NewsBTC reported on Coinbase’s CFTC registration for its USDC-focused derivatives clearinghouse, illustrating how cryptocurrency businesses are increasingly operating within established regulatory frameworks. The latest advisory gives relevant institutions another reason to evaluate how digital assets fit into their balance sheets. Still, there is a considerable difference between allowing an institution to hold Bitcoin for regulatory purposes and giving it an economic incentive to buy more. An exchange that already owns Bitcoin could benefit from the clarification without purchasing a single additional coin. Another might conclude that holding conventional securities remains more efficient, particularly given the valuation discounts and separate liquidity requirements. Nothing in the advisory requires institutions to acquire Bitcoin, and no purchase commitments were disclosed alongside the announcement. Investors should therefore resist the temptation to translate this development directly into a bullish price forecast. The longer-term significance may be greater than the immediate market impact. Every additional recognized use for Bitcoin within regulated financial markets strengthens the case for its utility beyond speculative trading. However, the November 23 document remains a staff advisory rather than a binding rule adopted by the full Commission. It does not amend existing regulations or create enforceable rights. The next meaningful development will be evidence that regulated institutions are actually changing their reserve allocations in response. Until then, Bitcoin has gained another form of regulatory recognition. Whether it gains another source of sustained buying pressure is a different question entirely.

title: Solana Price Prediction 2030: Is $2,000 SOL Still on the Table After a 75% Crash?
summary: Key takeaways SOL trades near $73, roughly 75% below its January 2025 high of $294, and tracked Binance whale positioning leans bearish (about 20% longs) while around 79% of broader accounts are long. PumpGlass shows a $19.5 million short-liquidation cluster near $79.01 and long-liquidation clusters near $69.39 and $68.01. Bitwise’s $385 base case depends on tokenized-stock trading, and a $2,000 SOL would imply about $1.38 trillion in total-supply value under NewsBTC’s 690 million-token assumption. NewsBTC’s conditional 2030 scenarios are bearish $40–$110, base $180–$400, bullish $600–$1,000 and extreme upside $1,500–$2,000+. Solana has lost roughly 75% of its value since reaching an all-time high of $294 in January 2025. Large futures traders are leaning bearish, yet institutional analysts continue to see a future in which SOL trades at four digit prices. So, how realistic is a $2,000 Solana price prediction for 2030? At around $73, SOL is trading at a fraction of the price some of Wall Street’s most optimistic forecasts suggest it could eventually reach. But a steep discount to an analyst’s target does not necessarily make an asset cheap. NewsBTC examined liquidation heatmaps, whale positions, historical price action, network economics and institutional valuation models to understand where Solana stands today and what it could realistically be worth by the end of the decade. The findings paint a more complicated picture than either bulls or bears might expect. Solana Whales Are Betting Against the Crowd Perhaps the most interesting signal right now comes from the derivatives market. According to a November 23 snapshot from PumpGlass, only around 20% of the tracked Binance whale position value was allocated to longs. Meanwhile, approximately 79% of the broader trader accounts were positioned long. Although the two figures measure different aspects of market positioning, the divergence is striking. Large traders appear considerably less optimistic than the wider trading crowd. The average entry price of tracked whale shorts stood near $77.63, compared with $77.05 for whale longs. With SOL trading around $73 at the time of observation, the short side was better positioned. Binance whale and trader positioning for SOL. Source: PumpGlass, November 23, 2026. The on-chain picture offers another reason for caution. On November 19, blockchain tracker Lookonchain reported that two large holders had unstaked a combined 2.31 million SOL worth approximately $169.4 million before transferring the tokens to Coinbase Prime-associated addresses. Exchange deposits do not necessarily mean those tokens were sold. Institutional investors use custody platforms for several purposes, including collateral management and portfolio rebalancing. Still, the movement is worth monitoring. What matters now is whether large holders begin accumulating again or whether the recent decline has further to run. A $19.5 Million Liquidation Cluster Could Influence SOL’s Next Move Solana’s liquidation heatmap reveals an interesting battle developing around its current trading range. PumpGlass identified several concentrations of potentially vulnerable leveraged positions in its November 23, 19:22 UTC observation. Price level Estimated liquidation exposure $79.01 $19.5 million in shorts $69.39 $10.7 million in longs $68.01 $15.1 million in longs SOLUSDT seven-day liquidation heatmap. Source: PumpGlass, November 23, 2026. Modeled estimates, not guaranteed orders. A recovery toward $79 could put considerable pressure on short sellers. Conversely, a breakdown below $69 could expose another wave of leveraged longs to forced closures. Data from CoinGlass adds another layer to the picture. At 21:31 UTC on November 23, Solana’s futures open interest stood at $3.86 billion, while rolling 24-hour liquidations reached approximately $30.59 million. Shorts accounted for roughly 72% of those liquidations. SOL had gained around 3.1% over the same rolling period. The recovery is consistent with some bearish positions being forced out of the market. However, a liquidated short is not the same as a new investor buying SOL for the next four years. Until stronger spot demand emerges, traders should be careful about interpreting a short squeeze as the beginning of a sustainable recovery. Liquidation concentrations are modeled estimates, not guaranteed future orders, and can change considerably as traders adjust their positions. Solana Technical Analysis: The Levels That Could Change Everything Solana’s price structure has deteriorated considerably since its September recovery. After closing July near $72.79, SOL climbed to $103 in August and $117.99 in September. The recovery subsequently unraveled, with October closing near $95.35 before prices returned to the low $70s in November. Solana (SOL) price chart, 2026. Source: Binance SOLUSDT, TradingView. Looking at SOL’s historical price action on Binance, using the TradingView SOLUSDT market as the chart reference, five key price regions stand out: SOL price Technical significance $60–$65 Major downside reference $69–$71 Immediate support $75–$80 short term resistance $88–$95 Intermediate recovery zone $100–$118 Broader trend recovery territory The daily Relative Strength Index was in the low 30s in the observed CoinGlass data, suggesting weak momentum and proximity to oversold territory. But oversold markets can remain oversold. A sustained recovery above $80 would be the first encouraging development. Reclaiming $95 and subsequently $100 would provide stronger evidence that buyers are regaining control. On the downside, failure to hold the $65 range would bring Solana’s 2026 low near $60.42 back into focus. Our technical assessment remains cautious. There is room for a meaningful relief rally, particularly given the nearby short-liquidation exposure, but the broader market structure has yet to establish a convincing reversal. The $73 Token Behind a Multibillion-Dollar Economy While Solana’s price has struggled, its blockchain continues to facilitate substantial financial activity. According to DefiLlama, Solana’s November 23 network metrics included: Network metric Reported value DeFi total value locked $4.68 billion Stablecoin market capitalization $13.14 billion Daily DEX trading volume $1.12 billion Daily active addresses 1.8 million Daily transactions 83.42 million Daily application revenue $2.07 million Daily chain revenue $23,978 There is something particularly interesting about those last two figures. Applications running on Solana generated considerably more revenue than the chain itself under DefiLlama’s respective measurement definitions. This highlights what could become Solana’s biggest valuation challenge. A blockchain can attract substantial activity and billions of dollars in trading volume without its native token capturing a proportional share of that economic value. Cheap transactions are excellent for adoption. Whether they are equally good for SOL’s valuation is another question entirely. That is why Solana’s expansion beyond speculative trading could prove so important. The blockchain’s growing presence in stablecoins, payments and tokenized real-world assets opens the door to financial activity that could persist even when speculative markets cool. Its infrastructure is also evolving. The Solana Foundation reported the activation of Alpenglow in October 2026, targeting transaction finality near 150 milliseconds. November’s introduction of Solana 1.0 marked another milestone in the network’s development. Meanwhile, the announced integration with DTCC’s Tokenization Service, expected in the second half of 2027, could represent a meaningful institutional opportunity. The real test will be how much financial activity these developments ultimately bring onchain, and how much value SOL captures from it. Wall Street’s Solana Price Predictions Are Surprisingly Far Apart Institutional research offers a glimpse into how differently analysts view Solana’s future. Research firm Bear case Base case Bull case / reported target Horizon VanEck $9.81 $334.70 $3,211.28 2030 Standard Chartered Not disclosed Not disclosed $2,000 target 2030 Bitwise $80 $385 $1,100 2031 VanEck’s October 2023 research produced one of the widest forecast ranges, with its most optimistic scenario placing SOL above $3,200. Standard Chartered’s Geoffrey Kendrick was reported in February 2026 to have projected a $2,000 Solana price by 2030, partly based on the network’s potential in stablecoin micropayments. However, the bank’s reported $250 end-of-2026 target looks increasingly difficult to achieve from current levels. Its original research note was not available for independent review. Perhaps the most interesting analysis comes from Bitwise’s November 2026 research, which connects Solana’s future valuation to tokenized stock trading. The asset manager’s base case assumes Solana captures 50% of tokenized-stock trading volume in 2031, generating approximately $6.75 billion in annual network economic value. Applying a 40-times valuation multiple produces an estimated SOL price of $385, based on a projected total supply of 700 million tokens. The report acknowledges the key dependency: “ Most of the price increase depends on how quickly stocks move onchain. Bitwise · November 2026 research In its bullish scenario, Solana captures 65% of tokenized-stock trading, generating approximately $12.83 billion in network economic value and supporting a modeled price of $1,100. These assumptions reveal just how much needs to go right before four-digit SOL prices become fundamentally convincing. The $1.38 Trillion Problem With a $2,000 Solana Here is something many price predictions overlook: Solana’s token supply will not necessarily remain where it is today. Unlike Bitcoin, SOL has no fixed maximum supply. Its inflationary issuance framework rewards validators and staking participants, while future governance decisions can influence the rate of supply growth. With around 592 million SOL currently circulating, we use an illustrative assumption of 690 million total tokens by 2030 for our valuation scenarios. The numbers put popular price targets into perspective. SOL price in 2030 Implied total-supply valuation $100 $69 billion $300 $207 billion $500 $345 billion $1,000 $690 billion $1,500 $1.035 trillion $2,000 $1.38 trillion $3,000 $2.07 trillion These are total-supply valuations rather than projected circulating market capitalizations. At $2,000, Solana would need to command a valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion under our assumptions. Using Bitwise’s base-case valuation multiple of 40 times annual network economic value as an illustrative benchmark, Solana would need to generate approximately $34.5 billion in annual economic value to support that figure. Even at a more generous 60-times multiple, the requirement would be $23 billion annually. That is substantially more demanding than simply attracting another wave of cryptocurrency traders. Our Solana Price Prediction for 2030 Based on the network’s economic opportunity, competitive landscape, token supply and institutional research, NewsBTC has developed four conditional valuation scenarios. NewsBTC original analysis: conditional SOL price scenarios for 2030. Editorial scenarios, not statistical forecasts. Scenario SOL price in 2030 Implied total-supply value Bearish $40–$110 $28B–$76B Base case $180–$400 $124B–$276B Bullish $600–$1,000 $414B–$690B Extreme upside $1,500–$2,000+ $1.04T–$1.38T+ These ranges are conditional editorial scenarios, not statistically derived forecasts. Outcomes outside these ranges, including substantially greater losses, are possible. Bearish Scenario: $40–$110 Solana remains relevant but struggles to turn network adoption into meaningful economic value for SOL. Institutional projects develop more slowly than expected, competitors gain market share, and speculative trading remains an important source of demand. Solana does not need to fail for this scenario to materialize. It only needs to fall short of the expectations investors have placed on it. Base Scenario: $180–$400 Our central expectation assumes Solana retains its position among the leading smart-contract networks while expanding its role in payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets. Under this scenario, the network does not need to dominate global finance. It needs to establish a durable position within it and capture more economic value from the applications it supports. Bullish Scenario: $600–$1,000 Solana becomes a major platform for tokenized equities, stablecoin settlements and high-frequency financial applications. Institutional adoption moves beyond announcements, network revenue expands significantly, and the broader cryptocurrency market benefits from favorable liquidity conditions. At $1,000, SOL would trade at approximately 13.8 times its November 23 reference price. Extreme Scenario: $1,500–$2,000+ This is where the most ambitious institutional predictions become conceivable. Solana would need to capture a significant share of a much larger on-chain financial economy, scale its infrastructure accordingly, and translate that activity into sustained demand for SOL. An exceptional cryptocurrency bull market could also temporarily push valuations beyond what underlying economics justify. We would not consider this the most likely outcome based on today’s evidence. The Five Signals That Could Make Us Raise Our Forecast Rather than following every new price target, long-term SOL investors may benefit from monitoring five developments: Stablecoin adoption: Growth in recurring payment and settlement activity beyond speculative trading. Institutional tokenization: Actual financial instruments and trading volumes going live on Solana. Network economics: Sustained growth in fees, economic value and demand for SOL. Institutional capital: Persistent ETF inflows and broader spot-market participation. Technical resilience: Reliable performance under heavy demand without sacrificing security or decentralization. Competition from Ethereum, its scaling ecosystem and specialized financial networks remains a considerable risk. If Solana’s transaction volumes rise while the economic value captured by the network stagnates, we would have reason to lower our valuation assumptions, regardless of how impressive the adoption statistics look. Is Solana Undervalued at $73? The current market offers an interesting contradiction. Solana’s blockchain has established a meaningful financial ecosystem, yet its token is trading roughly 75% below its historical record. Large futures traders are cautious, while institutional research continues to outline substantial long-term opportunities. Our $180 to $400 base-case range for 2030 reflects the possibility that Solana can grow without fulfilling every ambitious expectation placed on it. A move toward $1,000 is conceivable under considerably stronger conditions. At $2,000, however, investors would be betting on Solana becoming one of the world’s most valuable digital financial networks. The opportunity is there. The evidence that would justify such a valuation is not there yet. For now, the most interesting question surrounding Solana is not how many transactions it can process, but how much those transactions will eventually be worth to SOL holders. Solana Price Prediction 2030: Frequently Asked Questions How much will Solana be worth in 2030? NewsBTC’s analysis places Solana between $180 and $400 by 2030 under our base-case scenario. Strong institutional adoption and improved network economics could support a bullish range of $600 to $1,000, while weaker growth could leave SOL trading between $40 and $110. Can Solana reach $500 by 2030? Solana could reach $500 by 2030 if its adoption across payments, DeFi and tokenized financial assets continues to expand. Based on an assumed total supply of 690 million SOL, a $500 price would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $345 billion. Can Solana reach $1,000 by 2030? A $1,000 Solana price is possible under a strong bullish scenario. However, achieving and sustaining that valuation would require substantial institutional adoption, higher network economic value and favorable cryptocurrency market conditions. At $1,000, Solana’s implied total-supply valuation would reach approximately $690 billion. Can Solana reach $2,000 by 2030? Standard Chartered was reported to have projected a $2,000 SOL price by 2030 in February 2026. However, our analysis considers this an extreme bullish scenario. Reaching $2,000 would imply a total-supply valuation of approximately $1.38 trillion, requiring extraordinary growth in Solana’s financial ecosystem and demand for SOL. Can Solana reach $10,000? While mathematically possible, a $10,000 SOL price would imply a valuation of approximately $6.9 trillion based on our 2030 supply assumption. There is currently insufficient economic evidence to support such a valuation within this timeframe. Is Solana a good investment for the next five years? Solana offers long-term exposure to decentralized finance, stablecoin payments and institutional asset tokenization. However, its investment potential depends on whether growing network adoption translates into sustainable demand for SOL. Competition, token inflation, market volatility and regulatory developments remain significant risks. Will Solana overtake Ethereum by 2030? Solana could challenge Ethereum in areas such as decentralized trading, payments and financial applications. However, overtaking Ethereum by market capitalization would require substantial growth in Solana’s economic value, institutional demand and developer ecosystem. Higher transaction volumes alone would not guarantee that outcome. What are analysts predicting for Solana in 2030? VanEck’s October 2023 research placed SOL at $334.70 in its base case and $3,211.28 in its most optimistic scenario for 2030. Standard Chartered was reported to have projected $2,000 in February 2026, while Bitwise’s November 2026 research estimated a base-case price of $385 and a bullish price of $1,100 for 2031. What could cause Solana’s price to fall further? title: Trump’s Meme Coin Dinner Exposes a 94% Collapse in Holder Commitments
summary: Key takeaways Wallets on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held about $9.1 million at the November 16 cutoff, against roughly $148 million for the first dinner in May 2025, a drop of close to 94% in visible dollar value. That does not mean 94% of investors withdrew cash: the token price fell sharply, and the two leaderboards are not identical in size or method. The top 10 wallets held about 81% of the tokens on the public board, and the top 29 about 95%. Public Citizen traced 66 of the 130 displayed wallets to exchanges that restrict US customers, which is not proof about who attended. Donald Trump’s latest meme coin dinner came with a striking financial comparison: wallets displayed on the official $TRUMP dinner leaderboard held approximately $9.1 million in tokens at the November 16 cutoff, compared with roughly $148 million associated with the first dinner in May 2025. That puts the decline in the publicly measured dollar value at close to 94%. It does not mean investors withdrew 94% of their cash, or that 94% fewer people turned up for dinner. Trump hosted the third event for major $TRUMP holders at his Virginia golf club on Sunday, November 22. The gathering itself was new, but the more interesting story is what the leaderboard reveals about a token that was once able to turn a private invitation into a market-wide buying contest. NewsBTC previously covered an earlier $TRUMP meme coin dinner rally. This time, the numbers tell a considerably less flattering story about the value attached to that privilege. What the 94% Figure Actually Measures The roughly $9.1 million estimate comes from Public Citizen’s November 22 review of the 130 wallets displayed on the final public leaderboard. Its researchers counted 9,794,832.87 $TRUMP tokens and valued them at approximately $0.93 each at the November 16, 9 a.m. Eastern cutoff. The older $148 million comparison refers to the first gala’s leaderboard in May 2025. # Name Wallet Time-weighted holdings Latest $TRUMP balance Days held 1 FastX Dd54…uHDD 1,389,617.57 1,771,794.76 39.45 2 few DNLo…EoY6 1,093,044.76 1,000,000.00 35.75 3 Unitas Mhgx…itas 997,566.73 1,241,671.11 46.33 4 taotao BWgb…drJH 984,339.81 1,147,626.05 40.20 5 Yulia Gzyw…d6cp 966,503.35 1,126,182.24 40.23 6 GoTrump 3MwE…R1oS 453,211.23 459,963.62 46.34 7 FASTXCO H1fu…hh1c 436,614.04 700,002.00 29.24 8 ymca 8TUd…kg3S 137,348.63 140,000.96 45.98 9 3Eye 8DHk…qRjW 117,063.01 200,000.00 27.43 10 cl16 FNUY…Mts9 118,840.61 122,552.25 45.45 Source: Official $TRUMP Gala Dinner Leaderboard (November 16, 2026). Rankings based on time-weighted token holdings. Wallet entries do not necessarily represent individual attendees. That works out to a decline of roughly 93.9%, rounded to 94%. But the events did not have identical leaderboard sizes or necessarily identical valuation methods. More importantly, the token’s price fell dramatically between the two events. A lower marked-to-market balance can reflect falling prices even if some holders retain comparable token quantities. Calling this a 94% collapse in new investment would therefore be wrong. The narrower conclusion is still hard to ignore: the value represented by the public competition for dinner access is a small fraction of what it was at the first event. The leaderboard also should not be mistaken for a headcount. While the public display showed 130 wallets, organizers said 185 wallets qualified under the event’s rules. One person can control multiple wallets, and a wallet can be held for an organization. Neither figure identifies exactly who attended Sunday night’s dinner. A Few Wallets Still Control Most of the Leaderboard The smaller overall value is only part of the picture. Public Citizen found that the top 10 wallets held about 81% of the tokens on the public board. The top 29 accounted for approximately 95%. Those top-ranked wallets were also eligible for a special VIP reception. The concentration matters because a leaderboard is marketed as a contest between investors, but its aggregate value can be dominated by a very small number of positions. Looking at the $9.1 million as if it represented broad, evenly distributed enthusiasm would be as misleading as treating all 130 wallet entries as separate people. There is a revealing detail near the bottom of Public Citizen’s review: the wallet ranked No. 130 held only 9.71 $TRUMP, worth about $9 at the snapshot. It qualified because the competition measured time-weighted holdings over the scoring period, rather than the balance left in the wallet at the very end. That is perfectly compatible with the rules. It also shows why a dinner ranking cannot be read as a simple list of fresh purchases or long-term conviction. There is another market point here. A buyer who wants dinner access can acquire the token and hedge some of the price risk elsewhere. Holding a spot position long enough to earn a place does not necessarily make someone a directional believer in the coin. In that sense, the competition measures an incentive to qualify, not a clean vote of confidence in future returns. The Wallet Trail Raises Questions, Not Conclusions About Guests Public Citizen’s researchers traced 66 of the 130 displayed wallets, or 51%, to direct transfers from exchanges that restrict US customers. Those wallets represented about 4.35 million $TRUMP, roughly 44% of the public board’s token holdings. Among the top 29 VIP-ranked wallets, 15 had received tokens directly from such exchanges, according to the group’s November 22 findings. That is useful on-chain information. It is not proof that 66 dinner guests were foreign nationals, that all those exchanges served prohibited customers, or that any particular attendee broke a rule. An exchange withdrawal identifies a source of tokens, not a passport or the identity of the person controlling the receiving wallet. Public Citizen put a basic transparency problem plainly: “The names of the invitees have not been disclosed.” That sentence matters because a wallet address, however transparent its transaction history, cannot supply the accountability that a named guest list would provide. The event’s official website states: “ GetTrumpMemes.com is not political and has nothing to do with any political campaign or any political office or governmental agency. GetTrumpMemes.com · Official website That is the organizers’ characterization. It does not remove the transparency question created when holders of a president-linked digital asset can compete for personal access to the president. Neither does that question, by itself, prove an improper exchange of favors. The Dinner Still Has Value. The Token’s Investment Case Is Another Matter. There is a credible bullish counterargument. An exclusive dinner is a limited, experience driven reward. Its value to attendees need not move in lockstep with the coin’s market capitalization, and falling token prices can make it cheaper for new participants to qualify. The gala went ahead, and its promoters continue to offer other experiences to holders. But that is precisely why we should be careful about treating an invitation contest as evidence of a durable investment base. Access is an incentive. It is not a claim on business earnings, and it does not put a floor under the price of the coin. The most uncomfortable part of this comparison for $TRUMP holders is not that the dinner was smaller or less glamorous. The available figures do not establish either claim. It is that the token’s most recognizable promotional feature remains personal access, while the dollar value visible on the public leaderboard has fallen dramatically since the first event. In our view, that weakens the argument that repeated celebrity events, by themselves, can sustain the market’s appetite for the token. A more persuasive sign of recovering demand would be durable, independently observable holdings beyond a contest period, with less dependence on a few top-ranked wallets. The next useful data would be post-event wallet balances and exchange flows, measured against the November 16 snapshot, not just another photograph from the dinner. For now, the 94% comparison is a warning about the dollar value of the visible leaderboard, not proof of a 94% investor exodus. That distinction makes the story more credible, and no less troubling for anyone relying on the dinner promotion as an investment thesis. title: Fusionist ACE Bridge Exploit: $5.7M Loss Estimate, Bithumb Freezes Trading
summary: Key takeaways The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit is estimated at $5.7 million across two stages, according to SlowMist, which is not an audited final total. About $1.87 million in proceeds was traced to the attacker, while 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued near $3.7 million, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. Bithumb halted ACE trading on November 23 after finding signs that abnormally issued ACE had entered exchanges. In the material reviewed, Fusionist has not published a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem. The Fusionist ACE bridge exploit has produced an estimated $5.7 million in losses across two stages, according to SlowMist’s incident tracker. After unbacked ACE tokens were minted on BNB Chain and sold, traders reportedly used the resulting price collapse to withdraw real ACE from the project’s Endurance bridge reserves. The fallout reached centralized exchanges on Monday, November 23: Bithumb halted ACE trading after finding indications that abnormally issued tokens had entered crypto exchanges. This was not one attacker walking away with $5.7 million in a single transaction. The distinction matters. Roughly $1.87 million was traced through the attacker’s proceeds, while another 53.7 million genuine ACE tokens, valued around $3.7 million at the incident’s reference prices, were reportedly withdrawn through the bridge. SlowMist lists a combined $5.7 million loss estimate, not an audited final total. The bridge’s most basic promise, that a token issued on one chain corresponds to something real on another, is precisely what now needs proving. A Privileged Minter Printed Tokens That Had No Backing Security firm Blockaid flagged the Fusionist bridge-minter exploit on November 22. Its alert described the mechanism bluntly: “ A privileged token-bridge minter minted unbacked ACE and sold it for USDT. Blockaid · November 22 alert The firm initially estimated that about $1.04 million had been extracted while the attack was still ongoing. That was an interim snapshot, not a cap on the damage. Blockchain-monitoring account Onchain Lens subsequently reported that an attacker had routed 1,091.5 ETH, valued at about $1.87 million at the time, through Tornado Cash. That observation traces a movement of proceeds, not an extra $1.87 million to add on top of the initial extraction estimate. The values describe different points in the same suspected attacker’s fund flow. Fusionist acknowledged an apparent ongoing ACE exploit on BNB Smart Chain on Sunday and asked users to suspend transfers, trading and bridging on that network. It has not, in the material reviewed, provided a reconciled loss figure or a technical post-mortem identifying how the privileged minting authority was abused. A bridge minter is supposed to create a token representation only when the corresponding value is properly accounted for. Once the right to mint is misused, a chain can show perfectly ordinary-looking balances that have no matching backing. It is a familiar failure mode: NewsBTC previously covered a bridge-role exploit that minted unbacked tokens at CrediX. That earlier case does not establish Fusionist’s root cause, but it illustrates why elevated bridge permissions are such a consequential security boundary. Traders Found a Second Exit Through Real ACE Reserves The subsequent drain may prove more important than the initial minting spree. According to SlowMist’s November 22 incident entry, traders bought the sharply discounted ACE created by the market disruption and used the cross-chain bridge to withdraw about 53.7 million genuine ACE from the Endurance-side reserves. SlowMist valued that withdrawal at approximately $3.7 million. Here is the mechanism without the jargon. A representation of ACE on BNB Chain suddenly became cheap because unauthorized supply had flooded the market. A bridge that would still accept those tokens in exchange for ACE on Endurance offered an obvious difference in value. Anyone able to complete that conversion could receive real tokens in return for deeply discounted ones. The trading opportunity existed because the backing and the circulating representation were no longer in a trustworthy relationship. The $3.7 million figure is a valuation of the ACE reserve outflow, not proof that every recipient sold those tokens for $3.7 million in cash. Nor does it mean every trader involved helped compromise the minter. There is a meaningful difference between initiating the security breach and trading through a system whose defenses have already failed. Those distinctions should not obscure the core problem. A bridge can have technically valid transactions and still produce an economically disastrous result. If unbacked supply can be redeemed for genuine reserves, the checks have failed where they matter most. Bithumb’s Monday Halt Shows How Far the Problem Travelled Bithumb suspended ACE deposits and withdrawals early on November 23. It then halted trading effective 7:30 a.m. Korea time, according to its follow-up ACE security notice. The exchange said, in a translation from its Korean announcement, that it had: “ confirmed indications that abnormally issued ACE had entered cryptocurrency exchanges. Bithumb · ACE security notice It identified two related BNB Chain transactions and a second transaction. Those records are important evidence leads, but a full independent decoding of the transaction trail remains outstanding. Bithumb’s wording is careful: it reported signs of abnormal supply entering exchanges, not a finding that every ACE token in customer accounts is invalid. The trading suspension is a protective response, not a finalized determination of customer losses. Still, it creates a practical problem for holders who never used the bridge. If tokens are fungible within a market, exchanges and the issuer need a credible method for identifying affected supply and deciding how deposits, balances and trades will be treated. The Real Security Question Is Why the Bridge Could Honor the Claims There is an understandable temptation to focus on the enormous minting figures. The more consequential question is what happened when those tokens met the bridge’s reserves. A system does not need to lose control of its entire blockchain to suffer a serious failure in one privileged contract role. Nor should a successful-looking bridge transaction count as evidence that the asset being transferred was fully backed. Our assessment The response cannot end with a pause notice and a promise to investigate. Fusionist needs to show which minting permissions were affected, whether they have been revoked, how much ACE was created without backing, how the Endurance-side reserve changed and what claims remain outstanding. Exchanges need a defensible token-treatment plan, and holders need to know whether there is a shortfall and who is responsible for covering it. There is a fair counterargument: the $5.7 million figure is an external estimate, market prices moved during the incident, and the precise compromise method is not established. SlowMist categorizes the incident as private-key leakage, but that classification is not a substitute for an official technical finding. It would also be premature to treat a cautious exchange halt as proof that every affected customer suffered a loss. Those qualifications change how the numbers should be reported. They do not make the underlying bridge-accounting failure less serious. The next credible milestone is not a restored interface or a reassuring social post. It is a transparent reconciliation of the tokens minted, the reserves withdrawn and the assets still available to back legitimate ACE claims. Until that exists, the estimated $5.7 million fallout remains a warning about both token security and the risks of trusting a bridge’s accounting. title: Banks Are Adopting Stablecoins: Here Is Why Crypto-Native Dollars Still Win on User Freedom
summary: As traditional giants rush into digital dollars, USDD’s Yvonne Chia explains why 24/7 access, self-custody, and transparent yield give decentralized stablecoins an edge banks can’t replicate. 20 November – Road Town, Totorla, British Virgin Islands – Decentralized stablecoin protocol USDD is accelerating its multichain utility across TRON, Ethereum, and BNB Chain—combining automated sUSDD yield via its Smart Allocator with GasFree zero-TRX transfers—as traditional financial giants race to build competing stablecoin rails. In a recent industry interview with instant exchange partner ChangeNOW, USDD Head of Communications Yvonne Chia outlined why self-custody, 24/7 settlement, and transparent onchain reserves give decentralized digital dollars a structural advantage over bank-issued alternatives. 1. Permissionless Access vs. Gatekept Accounts For billions of people globally, opening and maintaining a traditional bank account still involves paperwork, minimum balance requirements, geographic restrictions, and approval delays. Even when banks integrate stablecoin rails behind the scenes, those services remain gated behind legacy compliance walls and intermediary control. Crypto-native stablecoins flip that model on its head. As Yvonne Chia highlighted during the interview: “Compare this to a stablecoin like USDD, where all you need is a phone, a working internet connection, you can immediately start a wallet and you have access to your funds right away.” With USDD, users can access and manage their digital dollars directly through their own wallets, without depending on traditional financial intermediaries. This represents a fundamental shift in financial access: users are no longer limited to the services, operating hours, or account structures of a single institution. Instead, they have the freedom to hold, manage, and transfer their assets on their own terms. Self-custody also gives users greater autonomy over their financial decisions. They can choose which wallets to use, where to transfer their assets, and which supported decentralized applications to interact with, without needing to route every transaction through a centralized financial institution. With USDD, users’ digital dollars can move with them across an open blockchain ecosystem, rather than remaining tied to a particular bank or service provider. 2. 24/7 Global Settlement vs. “Banking Hours” Legacy payment networks still operate on decades-old schedules: weekend cutoffs, bank holidays, and multi-day cross-border settlement delays accompanied by hefty wire fees. Blockchain networks never close. Whether it is a Sunday night or a public holiday, USDD moves globally without depending on traditional banking operating hours or settlement windows. “We are able to have transfers 24/7 and we’re not limited to any traditional banking hours. So I think that in some ways, stablecoins are not just becoming banks, but exceeding what traditional banks can offer to users.” To make everyday transfers even smoother than fintech apps, USDD introduced GasFree integration on TRON, allowing users on supported wallets to pay network fees directly in USDD without needing to hold TRX. This removes another practical barrier to stablecoin adoption: having to acquire and maintain a separate gas token just to transfer digital dollars. With GasFree, eligible users can pay approximately 0.5 USDD per transaction, compared with around 1.5 USDT for a standard USDT transfer under the referenced fee conditions. These improvements matter because the usefulness of a stablecoin is not determined by its peg alone. Low-cost transfers, straightforward wallet experiences, and around-the-clock availability are what make digital dollars practical for everyday payments and global value transfers. 3. Passing Yield Back to Users vs. Bank Spreads Perhaps the sharpest contrast between banks and decentralized stablecoins lies in how yield is distributed. In traditional banking, institutions take customer deposits, deploy them into yield-generating markets, and retain a significant portion of the returns. Everyday depositors may receive relatively low interest rates, while higher-yielding products often come with eligibility requirements, minimum deposits, or fixed maturity periods. Stablecoins introduce another way to participate in digital-dollar opportunities. Rather than keeping capital entirely within a traditional deposit account, users can access onchain yield opportunities through decentralized protocols and transparent investment mechanisms. USDD was built to return that value directly to holders. Through USDD Earn, users can deposit USDD to receive sUSDD, earning automated, competitive yield powered by our Smart Allocator system, with no fixed lock-up periods restricting access to their capital. For users, the distinction is important: USDD Earn provides access to a productive stablecoin while maintaining flexibility, rather than requiring users to commit their capital to a conventional fixed-term product. 4. Onchain Verification vs. Institutional Trust Traditional banks ask customers to trust closed-door balance sheets and periodic regulatory filings—until a crisis proves otherwise. USDD takes a different approach through its “Don’t trust, verify” ethos, emphasizing publicly accessible onchain information and independent verification. Onchain Transparency: Smart contract addresses, collateral reserves, and Smart Allocator deployments are publicly viewable, allowing users to examine relevant information directly on the blockchain. Structured Disclosures: Quarterly Treasury Reports provide additional information about reserve positions, financial performance, and operational developments. Independent Security Reviews: USDD undergoes third-party security audits to assess its smart contracts and identify potential vulnerabilities. Transparency does not eliminate financial or technical risks, but it changes how users can evaluate them. Instead of relying exclusively on an institution’s assurances, users have access to information that can be independently examined and verified. 5. Beyond a Single Network: An Open, Multichain Financial Ecosystem Financial freedom is not just about holding digital dollars. It is also about being able to use them wherever opportunities and applications exist. A stablecoin confined to a single network or limited use case cannot fully realize the potential of open blockchain finance. Following its January 2025 protocol upgrade, USDD expanded natively from TRON onto Ethereum and BNB Chain, extending its reach across multiple blockchain ecosystems. This multichain presence allows USDD to connect with different communities, liquidity environments, and decentralized applications. Its sUSDD product has also expanded into DeFi integrations, including Pendle and Morpho, giving users additional ways to access yield strategies across supported ecosystems. The bigger picture is an interconnected financial ecosystem in which users can move between holding, transferring, exchanging, and deploying their stablecoins according to their own needs. These are not isolated functions. Together, they make stablecoins more useful as everyday financial infrastructure. The Future: Interconnected, Open, and Multichain Banks will undoubtedly continue using stablecoin rails to modernize their back-end settlement. However, true financial freedom comes from open networks where assets flow freely across protocols without intermediaries. For USDD, the opportunity goes beyond offering a dollar-pegged asset. It is about making digital dollars accessible, transferable, and productive across an interconnected financial ecosystem. From self-custody and 24/7 transfers to flexible yield opportunities and multichain DeFi access, these capabilities give users more ways to put their money to work. Banks may be bringing stablecoins into traditional finance. Crypto-native protocols are showing what stablecoins can make possible beyond it. Watch the full interview at https://x.com/USDDecentralize/status/2121126175099773054. Explore the USDD ecosystem at usdd.io. Decentralized USD (USDD) pr@usdd.io
